mike: Heads-up from the qt-onboard run for kestrel-int4: we're seeing sporadic JSONDecodeError on toolcall outputs when the client retries immediately. error rate ~0.6% vs 0.01% baseline.

jess: Only streaming or normal too?

mike: Mostly streaming (SSE), but a couple non-streaming hits where the server returned concatenated fragments in one response. repro in mirror is easy with zero retry jitter.

mike: Sample symptom: first attempt ended with `...}}` then retry writes `{"tool":...}` and downstream sees `...}}{"tool":` -> JSON fails.

noah: Sounds like TCP coalescing + no explicit framing between attempts. Did this line up with any tokenizer/quant changes?

mike: yes landed with the int4 token boundary tweak. hypothesis: earlier stream termination yields shorter chunks and immediate retry writes more bytes into existing buffer.

irene: Proposed mitigations: 1) server-side attempt separator (SSE event or NDJSON lines) behind a canary flag, 2) client-side heuristic repair that extracts last complete JSON object, 3) require X-Invoke-Id idempotency header for tool providers.

jess: I prefer SSE event frame since hosted streams already support SSE. shouldn't break clients and gives explicit boundary semantics.

mike: built a lightweight client repair in node/python that scans for `}{` and attempts to salvage last object; recovered ~55% of failures in local sample. includes telemetry tag `repair_applied=1`.

noah: Good short-term, but we must avoid replaying side-effects. add X-Invoke-Id and X-Stream-Attempt headers so tool endpoints can dedupe.

irene: Action items:
- irene: prototype SSE `event: retry-boundary` server flag (eta 1d)
- mike: land client repair + telemetry in canary (eta 3h)
- jess: run 150k request canary with varied jitter and measure dup tool invocations (eta 1d)
- noah: add fuzz test that concatenates frames in the stream harness (eta 1d)

deploy-bot: deploy queued: kestrel-int4/qt-canary => host-group-canary at 2025-06-18T02:00:00Z (sha: a1b2c3).

jess: Make sure telemetry includes `repair_method`, `invoke_id`, `duplicate_tool_invoked` and we correlate with tool-side logs. If SSE reduces parse errors to <0.05% and duplicates=0, we promote.

mike: pushing client patch now. will post canary results to #onboard-results.
